title: A session reads the same whether it came from the list or on its own

expect.why: The reference configuration defines one session. A port whose defaults differ would leave every deployment's first experience different.
Which connector the default session uses is part of the default configuration, not of the port.
The input mode decides whether a viewer can type. A default that differed by port would be a security difference by port.
Who can see the session. Same reasoning as the input mode.
A configured session has no owner until someone takes it. Null, not an empty string and not absent.
Tags come from the configuration and keep their order — a port that sorted or de-duplicated them would change what a filter matches.
Recording is off unless asked for. A port defaulting it on would record sessions nobody consented to.
Its value depends on how far startup got, but a port that never reports lifecycle at all has dropped the field a dashboard reads.
The session named by the list can be fetched on its own.
Fetching by id returns that id.
The human-facing name comes from the configuration.
A running session has not stopped. Null rather than absent, so a client can tell 'has not stopped' from 'this port does not say'.
Nothing has gone wrong, and a port must say so rather than omitting the field.
